answer: A proof-of-cognitive-work protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve reasoning puzzles, such as verifying the structure of a complex sonnet, within intervals timed by a crystal oscillator. Because evaluating queries demands high-parameter model inference, an adversary incurs steep GPU compute and electricity costs per identity, reaching an expenditure zenith during mass attacks. However, this defense penalizes lightweight specialized agents and creates onboarding latency.
